summary.text: Tedi Rowland is the Democratic candidate for the Missouri House of Representatives, District 29, in the November 3, 2026 general election, where she faces Republican Robert Bruette.
A retired Jackson County government employee from Independence, she says she is running on public school funding, health care, disability issues and the cost of living.

paragraphs.text: Tedi Rowland earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Central Missouri and has a career background in communications.

In a Ballotpedia survey, Rowland said she had never run for office, is a mother of four adult children and a grandmother of three, and spent years volunteering with disabilities programs and in her children's schools after her youngest son was born with Down syndrome.
She said she is retired after many years working for Jackson County government.
Rowland advanced from the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026.

In the survey, she said she supports fully funded public schools, accessible health care, child care tax credits and subsidies, housing assistance for first-time buyers, and removing the sales tax on food and medicine.
She listed disability issues, public school funding, mental health services and the high cost of living as her policy interests.
